meaning.zh:
“幸运儿” 或 “走运的人”。

“Lucky dog” 这个短语最早出现在 1800 年代，最初使用狗来表示 “家伙” 或 “人” 的含义，加上 “幸运” 一词，就用来形容那些特别走运或幸运的人。在这个短语中，狗并没有贬义，而是配合 “幸运” 的含义，表示某人非常幸运或得到了特别的好处。
meaning.en: This idiom originated in the early 1800s. The word "dog" was used colloquially to refer to a "fellow" or "person" and, coupled with "lucky," it highlights someone who is especially fortunate. In this context, "dog" does not carry a negative connotation; rather, it complements the idea of "lucky" to describe someone who is very fortunate or has received a special benefit.

lines.en: He won the lottery again! What a *lucky dog*!
lines.zh: 他又中彩票了！真是个幸运儿！

lines.en: You got an extra day off work? You *lucky dog*!
lines.zh: 你额外多了一天假？你这幸运儿！

lines.en: She managed to get the last ticket to the concert, talk about a *lucky dog*!
lines.zh: 她竟然买到了最后一张演唱会门票，真是个幸运儿！
